extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers (wartime/news consumers); historians/researchers of contemporary wartime reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Dispatch-style newspaper reporting of military operations, home-front developments, and official statements during wartime; written for broad public readership. Focuses on frontline action, official casualty/loss reports, morale and civil-preparedness measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withhold sensitive battle news for public safety
rubrics_metrics.description: "No one in this country would wish to buy news at the price of a single British, French or Belgian life. We must all wait patiently and confidently till news can be given us with safety."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ministries and military authorities may hold back or minimize battle details when releasing information that could endanger lives or operations; reporters should respect official restrictions and prioritize safety over immediacy. Example: Ministry of Information holding battle news to a minimum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite official government and military sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and attribute statements from official bodies (Air Ministry, Admiralty, Ministry of Information, staff headquarters) when reporting operations, losses, and strategic developments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on named official dispatches and statements for factual claims (e.g., numbers of planes shot down, ships lost, bridges bombed). Make clear the source (e.g., "The Air Ministry reported...", "The Admiralty announced...") so readers can assess provenance and authority of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include frontline eyewitness and correspondent detail
rubrics_metrics.description: First-hand accounts from pilots, staff headquarters visitors, and correspondents describing actions, observations, and atmosphere (e.g., low-altitude dives, visible maps in headquarters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vivid, concrete details from eyewitnesses to convey events and scale (examples: RAF pilots describing dives at 200 feet; correspondent noting maps left on a general's desk). Balance dramatic description with attribution and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-check and qualify enemy claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not accept adversary reports at face value; seek confirmation or report denials from informed/institutional sources (e.g., German claim of sinking an aircraft carrier "denied in informed circles here").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When enemy or third-party claims appear, present them with qualifiers and, where possible, provide corroboration or official rebuttal. Use phrasing that signals uncertainty when verification is lacking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report home-front measures and civic responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover civil defense actions, morale events, and government domestic measures (blackouts, evacuation lists, prayer services, industrial mobilization, arrests of suspected fifth columnists).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the social and administrative impacts of war on civilians — evacuation areas, blackouts, hospitals, factory workweeks — to give readers a sense of national mobilization and daily effects. Attribute sources for official measures and include examples (lists of evacuation towns; seven-day factory weeks).
